Verdict: **ACCEPT_FIXED_MEASURABLE_FINITE_PATH_ALLOCATION_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY**.

FIRST_INCORRECT_ASSERTION: **NONE** in A0–A5 at the stated hypotheses.

The theorem is valid for the full certificate class actually defined in A2–A4: fixed measurable probability laws on finite paths, each with a nonnegative all-vertex-value slack, finite nonnegative charges, every occurrence included, and total charged measure dominated by the unchanged C_+. The law may completely redesign the old central allocation. This is a corollary/reconciliation of the September 5 translated-radical finite-stencil mechanism, not a new source-sign theorem or a literature novelty claim.

## 1. Exact source bindings and scope of rereading

Read directly for this audit: X's conventions, X/CONT, CAN/FT/ENV, EF, RAD and GS; C's inherited-object section and complete C3.1–C3.6, with its finite/global controls and scope; F's F1–F2 and F22–F24, measurable all-test interface and three-vertex control; R's initial intake/correction/acceptance section and complete S1–S3 and S5–S7 with the acceptance receipt; S's SL1–SL3 and the full-radical discussion. The relevant previously corrected FLOW statements were read as corrected in R, not by silently endorsing the old F15/F25 wording.

The published explicit formula behind X's radical identity remains the stated inherited PAPER dependency. The present proof does not need a new external theorem, a numerical value of a zero or slack, or re-execution of the old central interval certificate. This review checks the new deduction from the displayed analytic source results; it is not a Lean certification or canonical admission of their historical dependencies.

## 2. A0–A1: exact source, measure domains, and compact radical limits

The candidate's continuous coefficient is exactly the one in X/C/F. Indeed

`alpha(t)-2cosh(t/2)
 =exp(-5t/2)/(1-exp(-2t))-exp(t/2)`.

Setting this equal to zero and writing z=exp(t) yields z^3-z-1=0. The polynomial is strictly increasing for z>1, is negative at 1, and tends to infinity. Its unique positive root is greater than 1; the resulting tau is positive. The coefficient is positive on (0,tau) and negative on (tau,infinity). Thus the positive and negative measures have precisely the supports displayed in A1. Both pole terms have been retained, and Lambda(n) remains the von Mangoldt function, including its prime-power weights.

Because the full f is smooth and strictly positive, the negative density is strictly positive at every x and t>tau. Both measures are sigma-finite. For C_+, cover the receiving space by sets `|y|<=N, 1/N<=u<=N`: the continuous density is bounded on each relevant compact region away from zero, and only finitely many atomic lengths occur there. The same compact-region argument applies to D_-. Infinite local C_+ mass near u=0 is not a contradiction to sigma-finiteness.

The compact-test energies converge separately, as required for A1. Near zero the squared difference is O(u^2), while b_+(u)=O(1/u). At large lengths a nonzero difference of a compactly supported s requires at least one endpoint in its fixed compact support; the other f factor has the established double-exponential decay. This controls the continuous demand despite the growth of -b, and also the full prime sum. These are the source GS/F2 hypotheses, not a positivity assumption on Q. Division by positive smooth f maps every original compact smooth g to a compact smooth s=g/f, so the complex class is unchanged.

The radical input is a genuine bilinear radical. X obtains B(f,v)=0 on compact tests from its explicit formula and then on X by density and continuity. It does not infer the radical merely from the value Q(f)=0. Translation is bounded on X, preserves its difference energy and leaves Q/B invariant; the two pole moment factors acquire reciprocal multipliers and cancel. Therefore each f_q(x)=f(x-q) is a radical.

For the cutoffs of C3.2, `f s_(q,N)=chi_N f_q`. The error `(1-chi_N)f_q` tends to zero in X by the source derivative/decay bounds. Continuity and the radical identity give

`D(s_(q,N))=Q(chi_N f_q)=Q((1-chi_N)f_q) -> 0`.

The absolute NULL-BUDGET in C3.2 is stronger than the limit needed here. No sign of D was assumed to establish it. Each s_(q,N) is compact smooth because f has no real zeros. It agrees exactly with r_q on [-N,N]. These facts establish A2 as used below without evaluating the full form directly on the noncompact ratio.

## 3. Finite-value spanning for the full translated family

Fix any distinct real points z_1,...,z_k. Suppose a complex linear functional with coefficients d_j annihilates all the vectors `(r_q(z_1),...,r_q(z_k))`, q rational. Then

`sum_j [d_j/f(z_j)] f(z_j-q)=0` for every rational q.

Continuity extends the identity to all real q. Fourier transformation in q is legitimate since each translate of f is integrable. It gives the product of `hat f(-xi)` with the exponential polynomial `sum_j [d_j/f(z_j)]exp(-i xi z_j)`. Positivity and integrability imply `hat f(0)=integral f>0`, so the transform is nonzero on an interval containing zero. The polynomial vanishes on that interval. Differentiating it zero through k-1 times at zero gives a Vandermonde system at the distinct z_j, whose determinant is nonzero. Thus all d_j vanish.

This proves complex spanning of C^k, even though the individual sample vectors are real. It is exactly the finite-translate independence mechanism of C3.3; no sampling density theorem, real-zero assertion for xi, point-evaluation continuity on X, or measurable choice of a basis is needed. Repeated path vertices must first be identified as the same variable, as the candidate explicitly does.

## 4. A2: measurable path class and the total-charge measure

The countable disjoint union over finite m of the indicated finite-dimensional Borel spaces accommodates unbounded but finite path lengths, arbitrary finite vertices and charges, reversed edges and repetitions. Endpoint consistency with the demand is a measurable condition. A measurable probability kernel on this path space, integrated against sigma-finite D_-, defines a sigma-finite measure nu: the pullbacks of a finite-measure exhaustion of the demand space have the same finite masses because the conditional laws have mass one.

For each path, interpolation of arbitrary complex values at its finitely many distinct vertices is possible with a compact smooth function, by disjoint bump neighborhoods and complex coefficients. Consequently the two versions of the path inequality stated in A2 are equivalent. In particular its Hermitian quadratic slack H_p is positive semidefinite on the complete finite vertex-value space, not only on a restricted class of signals.

Each nonzero edge is sent to its left endpoint and positive length. This canonical unoriented coordinate agrees with the original C_+ coordinate, and the squared difference is unchanged by reversing orientation. Summing every occurrence with its finite nonnegative charge defines the nonnegative measure Gamma by Tonelli. One does not assume a common bound on the number or size of charges. Under the proposed domination Gamma<=C_+, Gamma is itself sigma-finite, since the same finite-capacity exhaustion works.

For precision, the residual `C_+-Gamma` in A5 is well defined even though the two total masses can be infinite. Domination and sigma-finiteness give a Radon–Nikodym density `h=dGamma/dC_+` with 0<=h<=1 almost everywhere; the residual is `(1-h)C_+`. This is not an undefined subtraction infinity minus infinity. It has the expected additivity on all nonnegative energy integrands. The notation in the candidate is valid with this standard measure interpretation.

The law and charges being fixed before choosing s or N is essential. The candidate explicitly imposes it. Test-dependent assignments and a sequence whose path law changes with the cutoff are not part of this theorem.

## 5. A3: exact decomposition, Fatou, and the PSD null argument

For compact smooth s, Tonelli identifies the charged energy with `integral sum_j a_j |Delta_j s|^2 dnu`. Since each conditional path law has total mass one and the path endpoints equal the demand endpoints, the demand energy is `integral |s(v_m)-s(v_0)|^2 dnu`. The former is at most the finite C_+ energy by A4; the latter is separately finite by A1. Subtracting these two finite values gives the integrated path slack.

Adding the residual-capacity energy therefore proves A5 exactly. Both terms on its right are nonnegative, and both are finite. Thus the hypothetical certificate implies, rather than assumes, `0<=integral H_p(s)dnu<=D(s)` for each compact test.

Fix rational q and use s_(q,N). For every individual path, the finite set of real vertices has a finite maximum absolute value. Once N exceeds it, every sampled cutoff is identically one. Hence `H_p(s_(q,N))=H_p(r_q)` eventually on that path. The threshold may depend on p without any problem. The pathwise limit is measurable, and Fatou applies to its nonnegative slack:

`integral H_p(r_q)dnu <= liminf_N integral H_p(s_(q,N))dnu
 <= liminf_N D(s_(q,N)) = 0`.

This argument requires no domination by an integrable function of the noncompact ratio, no uniform bound on vertices or path length, and no passage to a signed noncompact integral. It also does not require the cutoff energies to be monotone. Fixed nu and nonnegativity are exactly the hypotheses that make Fatou work.

The rational family is countable. We can therefore remove one nu-null set so that every remaining path has zero slack on all its rational-translate sample vectors simultaneously. For a finite Hermitian PSD matrix H, `z*Hz=0` implies Hz=0, for example by its finite-dimensional spectral decomposition or the PSD Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. Applied to H_p and the spanning result of §3, this forces H_p to be the zero matrix on the distinct vertex-value space.

There is no measurable eigenvector or basis selection in this reasoning: the matrix statement and spanning argument are used separately on each path after the common null set is removed. Variable finite dimensions are allowed by the countable union defining the path space. This verifies all quantifiers in A6–A7.

## 6. A4: off-diagonal necessity versus capacity support

With repeated vertices combined and zero-length edges omitted, every charged edge contributes its nonnegative coefficient times the usual two-point Laplacian. For the unordered pair of distinct demand endpoints {x,x+t}, the only contributions to the corresponding off-diagonal entry are minus the coefficients of occurrences of exactly that unordered edge. In the target endpoint Laplacian that entry is -1. Matrix equality A8 therefore gives exactly A9: the total direct endpoint-edge charge is one.

Neither an edge through an intermediate vertex nor a reversed orientation changes which off-diagonal entry it occupies. With nonnegative coefficients there is no cancellation from unrelated pairs. The stronger statement that all other total edge charges vanish is also true by their zero target off-diagonal entries, but the contradiction only needs the direct charge of one. Finite m ensures there is at least one positive direct coefficient; repeated occurrences simply add.

Let U be the candidate's set of allowed lengths. C_+ is concentrated on `R x U`. Domination implies `Gamma(R x U^c)=0`. By the definition of Gamma this is

`integral sum_j a_j 1_{length_j in U^c} dnu=0`.

The summand is nonnegative; consequently, outside another null set, every positively charged nonzero edge has length in U. No probability statement about an individual zero-weight occurrence is needed.

On the other hand D_- is absolutely continuous in (x,t), concentrated on t>tau. It assigns zero mass to the countable prime-power-length lines. Thus D_- almost every t is outside U. Probability disintegration transfers this exact statement to nu-almost every path. The measure nu is not zero: a bounded nonempty open demand rectangle strictly above tau has positive finite mass because its density is strictly positive.

Intersecting these full-measure sets gives a contradiction on a nonzero measure space. A9 forces a positively charged edge of length t, while t is forbidden on almost every path by the total-capacity support. This proves nonexistence of the entire A2–A4 class, even if every previous central or tail law is discarded and redesigned. There is no exceptional countable set of demand lengths carrying the missing continuous demand.

## 7. A5: controls, reconciliation and exact exclusion boundary

The three-vertex control is correct over complex values. With unit capacities on 01 and 12 and demand mass 1/2 on 02, path coefficients (2,2) use exactly one unit of each receiving edge. The source form is

`|z_1-z_0|^2+|z_2-z_1|^2-(1/2)|z_2-z_0|^2
 =(1/2)|z_0-2z_1+z_2|^2`.

Its null space consists of affine vertex data and has complex dimension two, not three. The pointwise slack is allowed to be nonzero on the missing direction. This satisfies the finite-path method without satisfying the rich finite-value radical hypothesis responsible for the canonical obstruction. The method is therefore not being refuted merely because a form has constants or another null function.

C's separate positive nonlocal control is also consistent with the conclusion: a positive form defined by a global Fourier functional can annihilate all translates of its chosen positive source and still have no nontrivial positive finite-stencil factor. Thus finite-stencil nonexistence is not an inference to original Q negativity. S's SL3 further excludes a particular class of L2-continuous square suppliers; A5 correctly keeps that separate restriction rather than claiming every nonlocal construction is available or impossible.

The older R conclusions retain the specific central slack and show that adding nonnegative residual domination, even after finitely many central-slack constraints, cannot complete that decomposition. The present theorem does not assume that law or those constraints. Its additional operational consequence is to rule out a complete redesign within the fixed measurable finite-path/nonnegative-charge/capacity class. Its underlying mathematical mechanism was already stated in C3.1–C3.6; A0 and A5 accurately describe it as a corollary and reconciliation, not newly discovered positivity mathematics.

The proper-subregion central and tail allocations in F/R are not contradicted. If only part of D_- is allocated, the identity for the whole D retains an unallocated signed part, so the resulting partial slack is not automatically a global nonnegative minorant of D. That is precisely where the present full-demand proof would fail for a partial law. R's corrected partial acceptance remains the appropriate reading of those older results.

Excluded: all fixed measurable laws in A2–A4 paying the entire original D_- with original C_+, with individual all-value nonnegative path slack, finite paths of arbitrarily variable finite size, arbitrary nonnegative finite charges and probabilities, and all receiving occurrences counted. Neither retaining nor redesigning the central law evades this result.

Not concluded: a sign or negative witness for original Q/V; nonexistence of signed global compensation; impossibility of a cutoff-dependent certificate sequence with proved vanishing error and fixed-test recovery; impossibility of every infinite-support or nonlocal factor; or impossibility of every argument involving paths. Such alternatives are not proved to work either. In particular paths whose individual slacks are not PSD, but which are to be combined with cancellations, are outside the stated certificate class.

## 8. Final disposition

The precise decision effect in A5 is justified: another search for a source-exact global capacity law in this same fixed finite-path class, including one redesigning the central law, would conflict with the proved obstruction. The all-test source-sign objective itself remains open and unchanged.

This is a bounded analytic PAPER review and accepts no Lean theorem, canonical theorem/consumer edge, RH claim or source-sign-counter reset. The only written file is this assigned private review. No source or candidate was edited, no shared or canonical state was changed, and no descendants, provider message, external research, numerical source evaluation, Lean run or publication was performed.
